name: DropdownMenu
purpose: Present a compact button-triggered set of commands, persistent choices, or secondary destinations while Atom owns menu semantics, focus, keyboard navigation, dismissal, and floating placement.
useWhen: An explicit button opens a compact set of commands, selection rows, or secondary destinations that benefit from menu keyboard behavior.

avoidWhen.condition: The content is primary site navigation, persistent navigation, a right-click-only surface, or a form selection field.
avoidWhen.useInstead: NavigationMenu or NavList, ContextMenu, or Select according to the interface job

composition: Compose Root > Trigger plus Portal > Content; use Item, CheckboxItem, RadioGroup/RadioItem, Separator, and Sub parts according to the menu job, and use Leading, ItemLabel, Description, and Shortcut for stable row anatomy.
Use Trigger asChild around a finished Brick Button or IconButton so the trigger retains a complete accessible name and finished control paint.
When a menu row is a destination, compose Item asChild around one real Brick Link and keep the visible item label destination-specific; commands remain action items with onSelect.
Place a direct Brick Icon, SVG, or image inside Leading and let the density-aware slot normalize and center its geometry.

rules.statement: Use Root, Trigger, Portal, and Content together and let Atom own focus, roving keyboard behavior, Escape, outside dismissal, focus return, and collision-aware placement.
Compose Trigger asChild around a finished, named Brick Button or IconButton rather than styling the behavior trigger as an unfinished control.
Preserve real anchor semantics for destination rows by composing Item asChild around Link; do not attach route navigation to a command-only div or button row.
Use Leading, ItemLabel, Description, Shortcut, and ItemIndicator for row content instead of application wrapper spans and alignment CSS.
Use tone=danger only for genuinely destructive commands and do not use danger paint as decorative emphasis.
Load styles.css or core.css plus dropdown-menu.css and every composed child component stylesheet.

commonMistakes.mistake: Hand-positioning a menu-like Surface, using Popover for command rows, nesting buttons inside menu items, or treating primary application navigation as a Dropdown Menu.
commonMistakes.correction: Use complete DropdownMenu anatomy for compact secondary actions or destinations, preserve one interactive owner per row, and choose NavigationMenu, NavList, or Drawer for primary navigation.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using an unlabeled icon as Trigger or rebuilding row icon/label/description alignment with custom spans and CSS.
commonMistakes.correction: Use a named Brick IconButton or Button as Trigger and compose the public DropdownMenu row anatomy.

validation: Test trigger naming, click and keyboard opening, arrow-key movement, Home/End where supported, selection, disabled rows, Escape and outside dismissal, focus return, submenus, density-aware Leading icon alignment, zoom, narrow viewports, and RTL.
Confirm command versus destination semantics, real anchor href values, danger meaning, collision-aware placement, light/dark appearance, forced colors, and complete CSS delivery.
